data.one_liner: High-performance asynchronous SQLite interface for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Wraps SQLite bindings to provide asynchronous database operations, concurrent read/write transactions, WAL mode configuration, and query watching without blocking the main isolate.
use_when: You need direct SQL query access without code generation overhead.
Your app requires high-performance concurrent read and write transactions.
You want to automatically watch and re-run queries on data changes.
avoid_when: You prefer a heavily typed ORM or object-relational mapping tool with code generation.
You only need simple key-value storage rather than a relational database.
strengths: Asynchronous operations by default to prevent UI jank.
Supports concurrent transactions with WAL mode enabled.
weaknesses: Web support requires additional configuration of WASM and web worker assets.
Does not use code generation or model classes by default, requiring manual mapping from raw SQL results.
data.setup_notes: Dart pub add sqlite_async. Web support requires access to sqlite3.wasm and db_worker.js files.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose drift if you prefer type-safe queries, relational mapping, and reactive streams via code generation.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose sqflite if you need the traditional SQLite plugin for Flutter with broad legacy usage.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose hive_ce if you want a fast NoSQL key-value database instead of relational SQL.
